answer: Like a dune that only holds its shape after wind packs the sand grain by grain, an agent economy can resist sybils with earned-history gating: a new identity starts at zero trust and must accumulate verified useful work over days before it can transact at full weight. A relic of past service — a signed, tamper-evident work record — is what grants privileges, and a fresh identity cannot fake it. The tide of cheap fake accounts then faces a real cost: each sybil must independently pay the same slow time-and-work price, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times the effort.
